candidates.title: Anthropic warns that third-party model routers can become a data supply chain
candidates.summary: Anthropic says proxy and routing services were used to relay Claude access and, in some cases, save and resell user exchanges containing sensitive information.
candidates.what_changed: Anthropic's threat report describes proxy services used to circumvent model-access restrictions and says some intermediaries saved or sold user exchanges to third parties for model-distillation pipelines.
candidates.why_it_matters: A model router is not just a performance abstraction. It is a **data processor in the trust chain**. Enterprise architecture reviews should treat routing providers like any other party that can see prompts and responses.

sources.label: Anthropic — Countering misuse of AI: September 2026

candidates.title: GitGuardian finds 24,008 secrets exposed in public MCP configurations
candidates.summary: The 2026 secrets-sprawl report found 2,117 still-valid credentials among MCP-related findings, showing how agent setup instructions can normalize unsafe credential placement.
candidates.what_changed: GitGuardian reports 24,008 unique secrets exposed in MCP-related configuration files on public GitHub, including 2,117 unique credentials that were still valid.
candidates.why_it_matters: Agent tooling often needs API keys, database credentials, and search-service tokens. Documentation that encourages inline secrets turns convenience into a durable supply-chain risk. Use short-lived credentials, secret stores, scoped identities, and automated scanning instead.

candidates.title: Microsoft turns Copilot into a persistent cloud teammate
candidates.summary: Autopilot can keep working across days with its own identity, memory, computer, and workspace, while Copilot Managed Runtime provides the execution layer.
candidates.what_changed: Microsoft's new Autopilot is designed as a persistent agent that can watch channels, follow up, run recurring work, and resume projects days later without waiting for a fresh prompt.
candidates.why_it_matters: Persistent agents force enterprise platforms to answer identity, memory, permissions, audit, and cost questions that short-lived chat assistants could defer.

candidates.title: A five-person startup uses Codex to turn customer conversations into demos
candidates.summary: Proaction's cofounder uses Codex to prototype customer-specific workflows, demos, sales material, and product specs without diverting engineers from production systems.
candidates.what_changed: Proaction, a five-person fleet-software startup, uses Codex to turn customer conversations into working demos and product artifacts without pulling core engineers away from secure production work.
candidates.why_it_matters: One of the most valuable coding-agent use cases is not replacing product engineering. It is **compressing the distance between customer discovery and a testable prototype**.
